children.translated_text: Obeisance to [Him] who bestows liberation (<s>kaivalya</s>), who is the embodiment of all auspiciousness,
to <s>Śiva</s>, the sun that dispels the darkness on the road of worldly existence (<s>bhava</s>). (1)
Free from the distinctions of absorption in all [competing] philosophical systems (<s>darśana</s>),
knowable only through self-experience (<s>svasaṃvedana</s>), abiding in itself — I bow to the supreme <s>Śiva</s>. (2)
To Him who destroys the flood of conceptual constructions (<s>vikalpa</s>) — the net of imaginary fabrication —
obeisance to <s>Śambhu</s>, who has transcended the state of supreme bliss (<s>paramānanda</s>). (3)
Victorious are [those teachings] that grant the discrimination of the essential from the non-essential in the boundless ocean of <s>saṃsāra</s>,
the feet of <s>Śambhu</s>, which are the cause of the awakening to the knowledge of liberation (<s>kaivalya-jñāna</s>). (4)
Mind, intellect, ego, vital breaths, subtle elements (<s>tanmātra</s>), senses, and the individual soul (<s>jīva</s>) —

children.text: yaṃ dṛṣṭvā vinivartante tam upāsyam upāsmahe //5//
children.translated_text: seeing whom, all these turn back; that one worthy of worship, we worship. (5)
The sole sword for cutting the heart-knot of 'mine' and 'I,'
which has devoured both movement (<s>spanda</s>) and non-movement — I bow to that pure consciousness (<s>śuddha-saṃvid</s>). (6)
How can one speak of that Reality (<s>tattva</s>) which is devoid of all designation?
Yet it can be reached by some, through the proper reasoning of self-experience (<s>svasaṃvedana</s>). (7)
One who has no inner confidence through the instruction of the yoga of knowledge (<s>jñāna-yoga</s>) —
being devoid of [such] assurance, how can the fruit of the highest good (<s>naiḥśreyasa</s>) [be attained]? (8)
The means to attain the goal is this: vigilant wakefulness in self-awareness (<s>svabodha</s>);
through vigilant wakefulness in self-awareness, the sage abides in an undifferentiated state (<s>nirvibhāga sthiti</s>). (9)
There is no other means than the pursuit of one's own being (<s>svasattā</s>);

children.text: tām evānusaran yogī svastho yaḥ sa sukhī bhavet //10//
children.translated_text: the yogin who, following that alone, remains established in the Self — he shall be happy. (10)
Through the examination of one's own intention (<s>saṃkalpa</s>), through reliance on purified knowledge,
and through the attainment of supreme delight (<s>paramāhlāda</s>), the sage [reaches] a dense concentration of pure awareness (<s>bodha</s>). (11)
When one's own intention (<s>saṃkalpa</s>) is restrained, [there is] the abiding of power (<s>śakti</s>) in the possessor of power (<s>śaktimant</s>);

children.text: śaktiśaktimator aikyam ity upeyaṃ ca yoginām //12//
children.translated_text: the unity of <s>Śakti</s> and the possessor of <s>Śakti</s> — this is the goal of yogins. (12)
When self-knowledge (<s>svarūpa-vijñāna</s>) has been attained, when the covering of principles (<s>tattva-kañcuka</s>) has been abandoned,

children.text: udyogakāraṇe kīrṇe muktaḥ sa kila kathyate //13//
children.translated_text: when the cause of [further] exertion has been dissolved — he is then truly called liberated. (13)
One should seize hold of pure awareness (<s>bodhamātra</s>) alone, with a fully awakened mind,

children.text: tāvad yāvat svasāmarthyāt svaniṣṭhaḥ kevalo bhavet //14//
children.translated_text: until, by one's own power, one becomes solely established in the Self (<s>svaniṣṭha</s>), absolute (<s>kevala</s>). (14)

children.text: sarvadā suprabuddhas san paśyaty ātmānam ātmanā /
children.translated_text: Being always fully awakened, one sees the Self by the Self;
for the seer who is established in his own nature — what else remains? (15)
Being always fully awakened — this alone is the dissolution of the mind (<s>manas</s>);
by that dissolution, the yogins' direct realization (<s>sākṣātkāra</s>) is fully accomplished. (16)

children.text: paryāvṛttaḥ svasaṃvittau vartate yas tv abhedataḥ /
children.translated_text: One who, having turned inward, abides in self-awareness (<s>svasaṃvitti</s>) without distinction —
he is the sovereign among those united in yoga, the sun [that dispels] the darkness of ignorance. (17)
Established like the moon in the state beyond the delight of the experience of one's own nature —
what remains to be attained here, for me whose inner organ (<s>antaḥkaraṇa</s>) has been dissolved? (18)
One whose repose in self-knowledge (<s>svaparijñapti</s>) is firmly and clearly [established],
for him, freed from mental modifications (<s>vṛtti</s>), the state of absolute isolation (<s>kevalatā</s>) comes swiftly. (19)
For yogins whose sole intent is the obliteration of the impressions (<s>saṃskāra</s>) of the grasped and grasping,
who are established in their own Self — the splendor of liberation (<s>mokṣa-lakṣmī</s>) is not difficult to attain. (20)
Repose in one's own nature has been gained; the stream of afflictions (<s>kleśa</s>) has ceased;
the duality of grasped and grasper is shattered — I am established, abiding in my own nature. (21)
The state of abiding in the experience of one's own nature through the awakening of non-dual awareness —

children.text: vyutthitaḥ sanniruddho vā labhate yaḥ sa tattvavit //22//
children.translated_text: whether in the active state (<s>vyutthita</s>) or in the restrained [meditative] state (<s>niruddha</s>), whoever attains this is a knower of Reality (<s>tattvavit</s>). (22)

children.text: yasya sarvāsv avasthāsu svasthitir naiva lupyate /
children.translated_text: One whose abiding in the Self is never lost in any state [of consciousness] —
what can the confusions of wandering through scriptures (<s>śāstra</s>) do to him? (23)
With the conceptual constructions of 'real' and 'unreal' dissolved, freed from the delusion born of the confusion of being and non-being,

children.text: jīvann api janamadhye vigatabhayaḥ sarvadā yogī //24//
children.translated_text: the yogin, even while living among people, is always free from fear. (24)
By whom <s>samādhi</s> has been practiced even once, with the senses withdrawn —
by that yogin, whose purpose is fulfilled, the Supreme has been directly realized. (25)
I, undivided in the Self, having gathered [myself] through my own effort,

children.text: prabuddhaḥ syāt svaniṣṭhaḥ san yāvat sādāśivadyutiḥ //26//
children.translated_text: should remain awakened, established in the Self, until [I shine with] the radiance of <s>Sadāśiva</s>. (26)
The knower, whose mental activity (<s>vṛtti</s>) is devoid of all objects and partless, having once gained the gain in his own Self,

children.text: samyaṅnibodhaikaparaḥ svaniṣṭhaḥ svakañcukaṃ hanta jahāti yogī //27//
children.translated_text: solely devoted to perfect awakening (<s>samyag-nibodha</s>), established in the Self — the yogin, indeed, casts off his covering (<s>kañcuka</s>)! (27)
One whose speech is endowed with the proper reasoning of [direct] experience, [and who abides] uninterruptedly in self-awareness —
it is fitting for him to give instruction to disciples, to truly awaken [them]. (28)
Through freedom from latent impressions (<s>vāsanā</s>), through self-awakening, through the renunciation of desire and pride,
through the severance of the categories of 'real' and 'unreal' — there is no further grasping of embodiment. (29)
With the inner organ at peace, with conceptual constructions dissolved, delighting in the attainment of one's own nature —
Satisfied by the nectar of self-experience, having fulfilled his purpose, he attains <s>kaivalya</s> (absolute liberation). //30//
Thus, in the attainment of the goal, free from impurities, truly illuminating consciousness (<s>cit</s>),
The <s>Svabodhasiddhi</s> (Attainment of Self-Awakening), the mother who gives birth to the glory of <s>kaivalya</s>, has been spoken by me. //31//
By which instruction one who has not [yet] obtained the gain obtains it, becoming sufficiently freed from the fault of doubt,

children.text: tenopadeśena nasaṃśayena kiṃ nāma kuryād bahuśāstrapāṭhī //32//
children.translated_text: By that instruction, without doubt, what could a student of many <s>śāstras</s> (scriptures) not accomplish? //32//

That which produces all auspiciousness, that which is a forest-fire for the [accumulated] various <s>karmas</s>, that which reveals the state of one's own true nature (<s>svarūpa</s>), that which is free from all conceptual constructions (<s>kalpanā</s>),

children.text: samastasukhamandiraṃ vividhaduḥkhamūlacchide namāmy asamasundaraṃ gurumukhopadiṣṭaṃ śivam //33//
children.translated_text: That which is the temple of all happiness, that which cuts the root of various sorrows — I bow to that incomparably beautiful <s>Śiva</s>, as taught through the mouth of the <s>Guru</s>. //33//
